name: Ser Benedek Orrin
epithet: Of Hollis's Sixth; the next cot
appearance: Not yet thirty, a knight of Hollis Garrow's own Sixth, on the cot next to his in the infirmary hall. A broad, open face that looks younger than its years: freckles across the nose and cheeks, ears that stand out a little, brown eyes under brows that lift in the middle as if an apology were always ready, thick dark-brown curls gone damp and flattened by the pillow, and a week's brown beard he has not been able to shave. A boar spear went through his shoulder at the ford and a fever came after it; the fever sits red and high on his cheeks, and the shoulder is wrapped like a parcel and tied with cord. He lies with his hands folded on the blanket and watches, with the eyes of a man who still feels a warmth in his chest, or says he does.
portrait_alt: Portrait of Ser Benedek Orrin: a young man with thick, damp dark-brown curls, brown eyes, freckles, ears that stand out a little, fever-flushed cheeks with sweat at the temples and a short brown beard, his brows lifted and lips parted, in a sweat-damp linen shirt with one shoulder bound in linen and tied with cord, a grey wool blanket pulled up to his chest, on a cot in a stone hall of cots with candles burning and snow at a high window.
last_seen_doing: Lay Hollowed in the Grey Cot; Rae was shown the frost on his mouth.
now: Lying Hollowed in the Grey Cot. The frost has not gone from his mouth in four days, with a brazier at his head.
story_so_far: A knight of the Sixth Lance who came back from Harrow Ford with a boar spear wound through the shoulder and a fever after it, and has the cot next to Hollis Garrow's at Saint Ysolde's. He says his oath at every bell. On the morning the grey cloaks were seen on the Holloway he asked Hollis what it meant to be second on the list, offered to carry him down the Steps himself if they would let him, and was told he couldn't carry a bucket, which made him smile. Hollis told him to say his oath and shut his eyes, and he did.

quote.text: I'd carry you down the Steps myself, if they'd let me.

known_facts.fact: He is of Hollis Garrow's own Sixth Lance, not yet thirty, and has the cot next to Hollis's in the infirmary hall of Saint Ysolde's.
A boar spear went through his shoulder at the ford, and a fever followed; the shoulder is wrapped like a parcel.
He says his oath at every bell, and says he still feels a warmth in his chest.
known_facts.evidence: the eyes of a man who still felt a warmth in his chest, or said he did

known_facts.fact: He asked Hollis what it meant to be second on the list and whether they would take him down, and was told that nobody was taking anyone up eleven hundred steps in the snow.
He told Hollis that if the Confessors did come up he could kneel, that the heralds had said it was mercy and only kneeling, and that he would carry Hollis down the Steps himself if they let him.
Told to say his oath and shut his eyes, he shut them and his lips began to move, and he did not see where Hollis put the folded paper from his shirt.
known_facts.evidence: Orrin saw what he was told to see; he always had.

known_facts.fact: He told the Captain the Grace forgives: kneel, and it comes back. Asked why mercy needs a list, he had no answer and apologised for not having one.
known_facts.evidence: Benedek had no answer, and apologised for not having one.

known_facts.fact: While the two captains played knucklebones he lay on the far side of Hollis's cot, and his lips began to move for his oath before either of them had heard the bell coming.
known_facts.evidence: Benedek's lips had begun to move

known_facts.fact: At the hour bell he asked the Captain to say the oath with him, only the words, since he cannot stand for it and the Captain cannot kneel; he said the Captain needn't, and that it is easier, two.
known_facts.evidence: Would you say it with me? Only the words.

known_facts.fact: He was not listening for the Captain's voice; he watched his mouth, and what he needed was the shape of the words beside his own. When they finished together he let his breath out and thanked the Captain to the roof.
At the dawn bell, as his lips began to move, his eyes went past Hollis to the Captain's mouth and waited there until it moved with his.
known_facts.evidence: waited there until it moved with his

known_facts.fact: On the night of the gate, when Hollis gave the hall the names read at the bars, his was not among them. He had lain waiting for it the whole time, and took it for mercy, as the heralds said.
At the night bell he watched the Captain's mouth through the whole oath and was satisfied, and said good night to him; the Captain answered aloud.
At the dawn bell of the feast he did not say his oath: he lay breathing, eyes open on the roof, with frost on his lips, and the hall called him Hollowed.
Under his tongue Maelis found a chip of black glass no bigger than a barleycorn; she said the far cots never had this.
known_facts.evidence: The far cots never had this

known_facts.fact: His cot, under the far cots' grey blanket, is called the Grey Cot; he was not moved to the far cots because Hollis would not allow it.
known_facts.evidence: the hall was calling it the Grey Cot

known_facts.fact: The frost has not gone from his mouth in four days, with a brazier at his head.
known_facts.evidence: The frost had not gone from it in four days

relationships.label: Ser Hollis, his captain on the next cot
relationships.note: He calls him Ser, asked him what second on the list meant, offered to carry him down the Steps, and shut his eyes and said his oath when Hollis told him to.

fire.state: borrowed and thin: a warmth he says he still feels
